where: Section 2, the line 'The pair |x⟩ + |x⊕s⟩ becomes Σ_y (−1)^(x·y) (1 + (−1)^(s·y)) |y⟩'
problem: The stated state has no normalising prefactor, so the expression is only proportional to the true state. A student who adds amplitudes directly will get a total probability of 2ⁿ instead of 1.
fix: Write it as (1/√(2ⁿ)) Σ_y (−1)^(x·y) (1 + (−1)^(s·y)) |y⟩, and note that the bracket is 2 when s·y = 0 and 0 when s·y = 1.

problem: 'the constant function is just the case s = 0ⁿ' can mislead: only the constant-zero function fits the Bernstein-Vazirani promise f(x) = s·x. The constant-one function cannot be written as s·x for any s.
fix: the constant-zero function is the case s = 0ⁿ; the constant-one function does not fit the Bernstein-Vazirani promise at all.
